knowledge_point.title: Finding the Slope of the Tangent at a Point of a Function Involving Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{11x}{sec⁡x}) \\  & =\frac{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(11x)\cdot sec⁡x-11x\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(sec⁡x)}{{sec}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{11sec⁡x-11x\cdot sec⁡xtan⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{11sec⁡x(1-xtan⁡x)}{{sec}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{11(1-xtan⁡x)}{sec⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=0$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(0) & =\frac{11(1-0\cdot tan⁡0)}{sec⁡0} \\  & =\frac{11(1-0)}{1} \\  & =11\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\sqrt{3}$ if $f(x)=23\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\frac{1}{x}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we calculate the derivative using the sum rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(23\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(23\operatorname{cos}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x+{x}^{-1}) \\  & =23(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-23\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $x=\sqrt{3}$ in the derivative and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\sqrt{3}) & =-23\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(\sqrt{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\frac{1}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =-23\operatorname{sin}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{sec}⁡(\sqrt{3})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
